title: The Ditch That Moved the World

lines.text: In 1869, a 193-kilometre channel through the Egyptian desert redrew the map of world trade.
lines.spoken: In eighteen sixty-nine, a one hundred and ninety-three kilometre channel through the Egyptian desert redrew the map of world trade.

lines.text: Before it, a ship sailing from the Persian Gulf to northern Europe had to go all the way around Africa.
lines.spoken: Before it, a ship sailing from the Persian Gulf to northern Europe had to go all the way around Africa.

lines.text: About 21,000 kilometres. Through the canal, about 12,000.
lines.spoken: About twenty-one thousand kilometres. Through the canal, about twelve thousand.

lines.text: Work began in 1859 and took ten years. In 1956, the canal was at the centre of an international crisis.
lines.spoken: Work began in eighteen fifty-nine and took ten years. In nineteen fifty-six, the canal was at the centre of an international crisis.

lines.text: Today it carries roughly 12 to 15 percent of global trade,
lines.spoken: Today it carries roughly twelve to fifteen percent of global trade,

lines.text: and about 30 percent of the world's container traffic.
lines.spoken: and about thirty percent of the world's container traffic.

lines.text: In March 2021, one container ship, the Ever Given, ran aground and blocked it for six days.
lines.spoken: In March twenty twenty-one, one container ship, the Ever Given, ran aground and blocked it for six days.

lines.text: At least 369 ships queued at either end.
lines.spoken: At least three hundred and sixty-nine ships queued at either end.

lines.text: One narrow channel, and a slice of the world's trade waiting on it.
lines.spoken: One narrow channel, and a slice of the world's trade waiting on it.
